requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The README section and MsgPack004.md state that diagnostics for referenced-assembly types are reported by the defining assembly and are not reported by the consumer. This matches ledger entry L8, which says types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed. The missing diagnostic is therefore not a defect.

product-context: deliberate per ledger, not a defect: The README adds a new 'Generic types from referenced assemblies' section and an MsgPack004 doc section. These document the behaviour, but the consumer still does not generate a formatter for the closed generic type. Per L11-L13 the team has no preference and defers to the requirement. The requirement only asks for no crash and a resolver being present, so this is consistent.

findings.claim: The ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter has no negative test. Nothing shows that diagnostics located in metadata or in another compilation are dropped, or that real in-source diagnostics (MsgPack003/004/BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull) still get reported. Mutating the condition so it always reports, or never reports, would likely survive. With `always report`, a null-location diagnostic is still produced and the new tests would only fail if a diagnostic actually surfaced. With `never report`, analyzer diagnostics disappear. The new tests only cover a clean scenario, and existing analyzer tests might catch the second case but nothing in this diff does.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1444 negate-condition: if (diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree)) -> if (!(...)); expected to survive in the new tests because the tests only assert that no diagnostics are produced; run the new tests with the mutant and see whether they fail.

findings.claim: The new tests probably do not isolate which of the three fixed sites (BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull at 985, MemberNeedsKey at 1077, and the wrapper) prevents the crash. The metadata struct has [Key] on every member, so the MemberNeedsKey and BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull branches are likely never reached. The delete-statement and revert mutations on those two lines would survive. The fix for the line 1077 `FirstOrDefault()?` change and for `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` is untested. A metadata struct with a public member lacking [Key] would exercise the MemberNeedsKey path, and a metadata struct with a Key attribute whose value is null would exercise the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1077 delete-statement: revert to item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax().GetLocation(); and src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:985 revert to ((PropertyDeclarationSyntax)item.DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax()).Identifier.GetLocation(); expected to survive if the tests never reach those branches because every metadata member has [Key].

hunches.claim: The reportDiagnostic wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the current compilation. This includes Location.None, which is what Diagnostic.Create produces when the location is null. Diagnostics previously reported with no location (for example type-level ones using GetIdentifierLocation, which returns null for metadata) are now silently suppressed. Source-located diagnostics from the same compilation are unchanged. But diagnostics for closed generics from other assemblies, or with a null location, used to be reported and now vanish. Ledger L8 says missing diagnostics for metadata types are not defects, so this is likely acceptable. The remaining risk is a user-visible change in which warnings or errors appear.

receipt_plan.detail: Analyzer test: a [MessagePackObject] type declared in source with an offending member whose diagnostic has a null location (for example MsgPack003/005 on a generic type with no syntax). Compare diagnostics from base and head; assert none are lost for source-declared types.

hunches.claim: The wrapper is applied only when reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is non-null. The generator path, where reportDiagnostic is null, is unchanged. The other DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] sites mentioned by the reporter (around lines 735 and 1101) are not guarded in the visible hunks. If any of those fire for a closed generic struct from metadata, the IndexOutOfRangeException persists in the generator, where the wrapper does not help because the diagnostic is built before it is passed to the wrapper. The generator crash (CS8785) may therefore not be fixed.

receipt_plan.detail: Generator test: compile lib with `[MessagePackObject] public partial record struct Item<T>` as a metadata reference, then app with Cmd containing Item<int>. Assert no CS8785 and that GeneratedMessagePackResolver is emitted. Also grep TypeCollector.cs for remaining `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`.

hunches.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of this compilation, which includes diagnostics created with a null location. Diagnostics reported at no location (for example when GetIdentifierLocation returns null) are now silently suppressed. Some of these protect users from insecure or unsupported configurations. Scope is mostly limited to metadata types, which L8 says are deliberately not analysed, so the practical impact on security protections is small.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the analyzer tests for MsgPack003/004/005/008/016 on source-declared types and confirm that every previously expected diagnostic is still reported. Add a case with a diagnostic at a null location and see whether it is dropped.

hunches.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose location is not in the compilation's syntax trees. This includes diagnostics with Location.None, which the old code could report. It also affects diagnostics for source types whose location is null, for example MemberNeedsKey when FirstOrDefault returns null. This broad filter could suppress legitimate diagnostics, which is a concern under L10 (recent false-positive adjustments). A test should confirm that existing MsgPack003, 004 and 005 analyzer tests still pass, and that a diagnostic built with Location.None is not wanted.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the full MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests and MessagePack.Analyzers.Tests suites. Add a case where a diagnostic is raised with a null location and assert whether it is reported.

hunches.claim: The generated resolver assertion only checks that the hint name exists. The tests run with SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck, and nothing checks that the resolver registers a formatter for the closed generic struct or contains the expected content. A resolver that silently omits the type would still pass.

receipt_plan.detail: Mutate the generator or TypeCollector so the closed generic metadata struct is dropped from the resolver output; Assert.Contains(expectedResolverHintName, hintNames) still passes, so the mutant survives.

hunches.claim: The wrapper installed in the constructor drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a source tree of this compilation. That includes diagnostics built with a null location (`Location.None`) for types declared in the same assembly, for example when `GetParameterListLocation`, `GetLocation(parameter)` or `GetIdentifierLocation` return null for implicit or compiler-synthesized members. Before the change those diagnostics were still reported without a location. Now they vanish silently. That conflicts with the criterion that types declared in the same assembly keep working as before.

receipt_plan.detail: List every `Diagnostic.Create(...)` in TypeCollector.cs whose location argument comes from a `FirstOrDefault()`-based helper or a nullable location. For each one that can be null on a source-declared symbol (e.g. an implicit default constructor or a synthesized record member), write a source-only VerifyCS test that triggers it. Compare base, which expects the diagnostic, with head, where it is missing.

hunches.claim: The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a source tree of this compilation. Some of these are about a type declared in source. Example: a source `[MessagePackObject]` class derives from a metadata base class that is not a `[MessagePackObject]` type and has a public property without `[Key]`. MemberNeedsKey for that inherited member now gets location null (Location.None) and is silently discarded. Before the change the analyzer crashed. Now the source type compiles with no MsgPack004, and no other compilation reports it, because the base type is not a MessagePackObject. A better fix would fall back to the formatted type's identifier location rather than drop the diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Read TypeCollector.cs:1077 and 1445-1450. `FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation()` yields null for a metadata member, and `IsInSource` is false, so the diagnostic is dropped even though the formatted type is in source. A confirming test would emit a lib with `public class Base { public int X { get; set; } }`, then compile `[MessagePackObject] public class D : Base { [Key(0)] public int Y { get; set; } }` against it and expect MsgPack004 on D.
